title: Jude and the Portrait
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Vale is exhumed for a heritage ceremony and found empty, concierge Quentin Dunmore realizes the guest register he has kept for twelve years contains the key: someone checked in under a dead man's name the night before the exhumation. As Quentin investigates, they discover the portrait hanging in the hotel lobby is not of Edmund at all, but of his twin brother — the man who actually founded the town and was erased from history. The killer, the town archivist who has spent decades protecting the false lineage, begins eliminating everyone who can confirm the switch, including Quentin's estranged aunt, whose inheritance papers prove the truth. In a final confrontation inside the hotel's sealed attic, Quentin traps the archivist using the very filing system she taught them, restoring the true founder's name and choosing love over the duty of silence.
about_author: Freya Dravenmoor spent a decade working night desks in small-town hotels, where she learned that every lobby keeps two histories: the one on display and the one in the ledger. She writes mysteries about people who notice too much, from a farmhouse office lined with other people's abandoned luggage tags.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Checked In Twice
chapters.summary: Quentin Dunmore, concierge of the Marlowe Grand, notices a guest registered as 'E. Vale' — a name that shouldn't exist. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath professional composure; the first crack in twelve years of orderly routine.

chapters.title: An Empty Coffin in Sunday Light
chapters.summary: The town gathers to reinter founder Edmund Vale after crypt repairs; the coffin holds only stones. POV: Quentin, watching the crowd rather than the grave. Emotional beat: collective shock, and Quentin's private horror at recognizing the gravedigger's face from the hotel registry.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Quentin reviews their private ledgers and finds three prior visits by someone using Vale family names. Detective Ilsa Reyes arrives at the desk, needing the records Quentin swore never to share. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: loyalty to guests versus duty to truth — the book's central tension ignited.

chapters.title: The Portrait That Watches
chapters.summary: Quentin studies the lobby portrait of Edmund Vale and notices the hands are wrong — a laborer's hands, not a financier's. Archivist Miriam Halloway dismisses the observation warmly, too smoothly. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the thrill of noticing colliding with the fear of what noticing costs.

chapters.title: A Name Scratched From Stone
chapters.summary: In the cemetery, Quentin finds a second plinth, defaced, beside Edmund's monument. The chisel marks are old; the concealment is new. POV: alternating Quentin and Ilsa. Emotional beat: two investigators circling each other, neither yet trusting, both needing the same answer.

chapters.title: The Aunt Who Left Without Packing
chapters.summary: Quentin's estranged aunt Corliss checks into the hotel under a false name, carrying her late mother's inheritance papers. She warns Quentin to stop asking about Vales. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: longing for family tangled with suspicion — is she protecting Quentin or herself?

chapters.title: Room 214 Keeps Its Silence
chapters.summary: The guest registered as E. Vale vanishes, leaving a room cleaned of everything except a pressed violet on the pillow — Edmund Vale's funeral flower. POV: housekeeper Marta, then Quentin. Emotional beat: dread; the case has stepped out of ledgers into flesh.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Ilsa confronts Quentin about a torn ledger page; someone with staff access removed it. Quentin realizes the killer knows their filing system intimately. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: violation — the archive that made Quentin feel safe becomes evidence against them.

chapters.title: Miriam's Beautiful Archive
chapters.summary: Quentin visits the town archive and admires Miriam's immaculate cataloguing — and notices gaps exactly where Vale history should be densest. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: admiration shading into cold recognition; perfection itself becomes suspicious.

chapters.title: Corliss Confesses Half
chapters.summary: Over brandy, Corliss admits the inheritance papers name a different founder: Edmund's twin, Tobias, the laborer in the portrait. She refuses to say who else knows. POV: Corliss. Emotional beat: tenderness and frustration between aunt and niece/nephew; love offered in fragments.

chapters.title: The First Body in the Reading Room
chapters.summary: The cemetery caretaker who opened the coffin is found dead among the archive shelves, an index card in his pocket reading 'misfiled.' POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; the killer is now communicating through the system itself.

chapters.title: Quentin Under Suspicion
chapters.summary: Ilsa must formally question Quentin, whose access and knowledge make them the obvious suspect. Their fragile alliance strains. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: loneliness of duty; Ilsa likes Quentin and cannot afford to.

chapters.title: The Twin in the Attic
chapters.summary: Following a maintenance lead, Quentin finds the sealed attic room where Tobias Vale apparently lived and died — and was written out. A second portrait faces the wall. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: awe and sorrow; the town's whole identity revealed as a curated lie.

chapters.title: Someone Is Filing the Living
chapters.summary: Quentin discovers index cards for themselves, Corliss, and Ilsa in Miriam's cataloguing style — each marked with a date. Two dates have passed. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: terror rendered bureaucratic; being reduced to a record awaiting closure.

chapters.title: Corliss Runs
chapters.summary: Corliss flees with the inheritance papers, leaving a note that reads like a goodbye. Quentin must choose: follow protocol or follow her. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal; Quentin chooses love and breaks their own rules for the first time.

chapters.title: The Night Train Interrogation
chapters.summary: Quentin catches Corliss at the station; she reveals Miriam Halloway is Tobias's granddaughter, raised on the erasure, and that the exhumation was meant to force the truth open. POV: Corliss. Emotional beat: pity complicating pursuit — the enemy may be grieving, not merely guilty.

chapters.title: Misfiled
chapters.summary: They return to find the hotel ransacked and Ilsa missing, an index card bearing her name left on the desk. The third date is tomorrow. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: guilt and fury fused; every careful habit now feels like complicity.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's Catalogue
chapters.summary: Quentin deciphers Miriam's classification scheme and predicts her next location: the vault beneath the archive where the original founding deed is stored. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: competence reclaimed — the weapon Miriam built is turned by its best student.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Town
chapters.summary: In the vault, Quentin finds Ilsa alive but bound, and Miriam waiting with the deed naming Tobias Vale as founder. Miriam offers Quentin a place in the corrected history. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: temptation — a cleaner world, if only the inconvenient people stay filed away.

chapters.title: Climax: The Alphabet Trap
chapters.summary: Quenton feigns agreement, then springs a trap laid through the archive's own call-number system, summoning Ilsa's backup while cornering Miriam among her perfect shelves. Miriam burns the deed rather than surrender it. POV: Quentin and Miriam. Emotional beat: the climax — order defeated by its own rigidity; grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Tobias Vale is buried under his own name; the twin portraits hang side by side in the lobby. Corliss signs the inheritance over to the town trust, keeping only the attic key. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: mourning turned to restoration; names given back to the erased.

chapters.title: The Concierge Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Months later, Quentin registers a new guest, notices everything as always, and chooses which secrets deserve filing. Ilsa leaves a violet on the desk — an invitation, not a warning. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: resolution — duty and love reconciled; the ledger reopened, this time by choice.
